children: Chicago Mercantile Exchange live and feeder cattle futures ticked higher on Monday as traders adjusted positions ahead of the expiration of the August live cattle contract
settled 0.95 cent higher at 212.675 cents per pound. CME October feeder cattle futures
rose 0.50 cent to 317.025 cents per pound.

The cattle market is pricing in a slew of bearish news in recent weeks – from the re-opening of the U.S.-Mexico border to feeder cattle imports to the U.S. temporarily waiving import tariffs for beef.
"We're digesting all the incredibly bearish stories from recent weeks and asking the question – is this enough," said Rich Nelson, chief strategist at Allendale.
Falling wholesale beef prices and a weak cash cattle market have also put pressure on cattle futures.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture priced choice cuts of boxed beef at $375.20 per hundredweight on Monday, down $1.03 from the previous day, and select cuts fell $6.57 to $354.51  per hundredweight.

U.S. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said on Monday that the USDA is taking actions to support the beef industry, including loans for small meat processors and the use of conserved land for grazing.
President Donald Trump on Friday pledged action to allow ranchers to process their own cattle, aimed at breaking up a "nasty monopoly" among top meatpackers.

U.S. shoppers have faced record beef prices as drought and wildfires have driven the cattle herd to 75-year lows. Trump last week signed an order expanding lower-tariff beef imports in an effort to bring down prices, angering farm groups.
The USDA reported wholesale pork carcass values at $95.16 per hundredweight, up $1.36 from a day earlier.
The most actively traded October lean hog contract (LHV26) settled 1.775 cent higher to 83.675 cents per pound.
